Evendale, the supplier belt and the river: how SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 divide Cincinnati NDT work

Cincinnati NDT jobs fall on both sides of a line most candidates never hear about. GE Aerospace runs its headquarters and engine engineering and manufacturing in Evendale, tests engines outdoors at Peebles in Adams County, and in March 2026 announced more spending in Cincinnati on test-cell capacity and metal additive manufacturing. A long belt of casting, forging, machining, coating and repair shops along I-75 feeds that work. Down at the river, steel, chemical, bridge and barge contractors inspect to construction and pressure codes. Which side you work on decides whether your certification is written to NAS 410 or to a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Who you work for decides the document

Where you work around CincinnatiScheme you will usually meetWhy
Casting, forging, machining or coating supplier to an engine makerNAS 410, or EN 4179 on European ordersThe customer names it in the purchase order quality clause and it flows down to every sub-tier shop that tests the hardware
Nadcap-accredited special process house running a fluorescent penetrant lineNAS 410 under a designated Responsible Level 3Nadcap AC7114 accredits the site, and its auditors trace each inspector's certification to evidence
Defense contractor working toward Wright-Patterson, about an hour northCommonly NAS 410, flowed down from the primeNAS 410 replaced MIL-STD-410 in defense aerospace buying
Cargo aircraft maintenance tied to the DHL and Amazon Air hubs at CVGWhatever the operator's or repair station's manual namesFAA does not certify NDT personnel; AC 65-31B accepts several standards, including NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 and SNT-TC-1A
Steel mill, chemical plant, bridge or river contractorSNT-TC-1A, sometimes CP-189ASME, API and AWS work calls for it through the employer's written practice
The engine maker's own inspection departmentsThe company's own written practiceAsk its Level 3 which standard and revision govern before you assume either

Neither scheme hands you a portable card. The employer certifies you, and the certification ends when you leave. What survives a job change is the evidence behind it.

Crossing from a river contractor to a supplier north of the city

The common Cincinnati move runs from weld and thickness work on the river to a supplier north of the city inspecting engine-type parts. Three things change. First, the shop's Responsible Level 3 (RL3) reviews your record and decides what earlier training and experience to credit; an SNT-TC-1A certificate is useful evidence, but it does not meet a NAS 410 requirement on its own. Second, fluorescent penetrant becomes the daily method, and NAS 410 expects more formal, documented penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, so surface-method hours are where most river technicians fall short. Third, your specific examination tests the shop's procedures and the customer's specifications, not general method knowledge.

Before you accept, ask the RL3 four things: which standard and revision the written practice follows, which of your records will be credited, what formal training you still need and in which methods, and how long until your first practical examination. Bring course outlines with recorded hours, a signed experience log split by method, your examination history and a current vision record. Our penetrant testing training and the guide to penetrant inspection of castings show what the surface-method work involves, and the free Level II practice tests let you check your theory first.

For quality managers in the I-75 supplier belt

Plenty of Cincinnati shops run aerospace orders and industrial orders on the same floor. Keep separate written practices or clearly separate sections, write the governing standard and revision on every certification letter, and schedule the move of your NAS 410 program to Revision 6, released in December 2025, as your customers require. Expect a Nadcap or customer auditor to pick a signed report and walk it back through the inspector's training, experience, examinations and eyesight records. Atlantis offers NAS 410 audit documentation support for Cincinnati suppliers, preparing and reviewing those records for your RL3 to approve, and builds aerospace written practices on SNT-TC-1A aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

What Atlantis does, and does not do, for Cincinnati

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Theory is self-paced online with Q&A from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT); you rehearse in the Practical NDT simulator; the hands-on work and practical examination happen at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Cincinnati. Our Level III consulting covers procedures, Level I and II examinations, audit preparation and outside agency Level III services in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 for Cincinnati-area suppliers. Credit for outside coursework toward a NAS 410 certification sits with the supplier's own RL3, so put the question to that person before you enroll. For the full comparison, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.
